summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — GPN +6%, LITE +4%, TER +4%, AXON +3%, MRVL +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HONA -5%, CVNA -5%, ORCL -4%, KKR -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: GPN (+5.85%) — Morgan Stanley upgraded GPN to Overweight, hiking PT from $65 to $100, citing improving Worldpay/Genius integration checks ahead of Q2 earnings. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — GPN is a large-cap ($22.5B) payments-processing/fintech name likely excluded because the bot's universe doesn't cover that sector, not because of a technical filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley upgraded GPN to Overweight, hiking PT from $65 to $100, citing improving Worldpay/Genius integration checks ahead of Q2 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GPN is a large-cap ($22.5B) payments-processing/fintech name likely excluded because the bot's universe doesn't cover that sector, not because of a technical filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sell-side rating-change gate that pulls large-cap financials/payments names (mkt cap >$10B) into the universe on same-day >30% price-target hikes from bulge-bracket analysts.

top_movers.catalyst: Barclays upgraded LITE to Overweight with a $1,000 PT, extending an AI-optics/800G-1.6T transceiver demand rally (stock +107% YTD) ahead of Aug 11 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely a stale universe list: LITE re-rated from a ~$370 small/mid-cap optical-component name to a >$700 mega-mover this year, but universe membership (cap/sector bucket) wasn't refreshed to catch the reclassification.
top_movers.suggestion: Refresh universe cap/sector buckets monthly (not quarterly) so YTD +100%+ re-raters like LITE get pulled into the tradable set instead of being filtered on stale market-cap tier data.

top_movers.catalyst: No single fresh headline; extension of a multi-week AI-testing rally (stock ~250% off recent lows) fueled by a wave of analyst PT hikes (Cantor $550, BofA $525, UBS $500) ahead of July 28 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TER falls in semiconductor capital-equipment/test, a sector/name class the bot's tradable list doesn't cover, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SOX-index semiconductor-equipment names (TER, KLAC, LRCX, AMAT) to universe scans; a sector-coverage gap, not a signal-threshold miss, kept this one untouched.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued multi-week rally fueled by bullish analyst coverage (Piper Sandler PT to $724, Needham to $750) and ICE/public-safety contract momentum; no single fresh headline dated today.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AXON is a ~$43B Nasdaq industrials/capital-goods name (TASER/body-cams/public-safety SaaS), a sector likely excluded from tech/momentum-focused universes, and its huge 52-week range ($339-$886) may also trip volatility caps.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a large-cap ($30B+) 'public-safety tech' carve-out to the industrials universe filter so idiosyncratic-catalyst names like AXON aren't screened out purely by GICS sector classification.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news; broad AI-capex/semiconductor rally (AMD's Helios launch stoking GPU/ASIC-adjacent demand optimism) lifted MRVL ahead of its Aug 27 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — MRVL is a high-beta AI-semis name only added to the S&P 500 in June 2026 and down ~37% over the trailing month, likely screened out by volatility/drawdown or recent-index-add filters before universe refresh caught it.
top_movers.suggestion: Refresh universe membership from S&P 500 constituent changes monthly (not quarterly) so recently-added names like MRVL enter the tradable set within weeks of inclusion, not months.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh company news — technical short-covering rally off oversold levels (RSI ~39, price below 20/50/200-day MAs) following recent Sazerac bid rejection/Pernod talks collapse volatility.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely; BF-B is a dual-class ticker (Class B non-voting, hyphen/dot suffix) in consumer-staples/spirits, a sector and symbol format the bot's universe ingestion likely doesn't cover or normalize.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend universe symbol normalization to handle dual-class suffixes (-A/-B, .A/.B) so shares like BF-B aren't silently dropped, and review whether consumer-staples/spirits names above a market-cap floor should be added to sector coverage.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news trigger; HONA drifted to a fresh 52-week low amid post-spinoff outflows and a broad aerospace/defense sector selloff (peers like Northrop down despite beats).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HONA only began trading June 29, 2026 after its Honeywell spinoff, so it lacks the 60-90 day price/volume history most universe-inclusion screens require.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a spinoff fast-track rule: admit new spinoff tickers to the universe after ~15 trading days once avg volume/price history minimums are met, instead of the standard 60-90 day lookback gate.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh single-day headline; continued slide from CarMax's Jun-17 margin/credit-loss read-through, Jefferies/RBC price-target cuts (to $90/$85), and insider selling into the Jul-29 earnings date.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CVNA is a high-beta auto-retail name still carrying headline risk from a Jan 2026 short-seller fraud allegation, likely screened out by sector or headline-risk/volatility filters entirely.
top_movers.suggestion: If CVNA clears cap/liquidity thresholds, add it under a pre-earnings volatility gate (exclude only within T-3 days of earnings) instead of a blanket sector exclusion, so peer-driven read-through moves like CarMax→Carvana get traded.

top_movers.catalyst: Continuing AI-capex/credit selloff after Jul 9 S&P downgrade to BBB- (OpenAI concentration, ~$42B FY27 FCF deficit); New Mexico data-center permit setback added pressure; fresh 52-wk low.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ORCL is a mega-cap tech name in a multi-week grinding decline (down ~50% since June), not a single-day gap/news spike a momentum or news-reactive scanner would flag intraday.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'crumbling mega-cap' watchlist (>25% drawdown in 60d + recent credit-rating downgrade) feeding a slow-momentum/short sleeve, so grinding de-ratings like ORCL become eligible if short capability exists.

top_movers.catalyst: Bloomberg reported KKR is selling 9 China commercial real-estate properties at ~50-60% of purchase price, just enough to repay the acquisition loans.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — KKR is a large-cap alternative asset manager/financials name not covered by the bot's tradable list, and the move stemmed from an intraday Bloomberg report rather than a pre-market gap or earnings print the bot's news-reactive signals scan for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap alternative asset managers (KKR, BX, APO, ARES) to the financials universe and wire a headline-trigger gate for 'asset write-down/fire-sale' language from Bloomberg/Reuters on constituents.
